items.ti: ITU-T P.IntVR: "Subjective Test Method for Interactive Virtual Reality Applications" - Social acceptability, test paradigm, experimental design and test environment for Interactive Virtual Reality - Quality of Experience aspects for Interactive Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojić, T., Vergari, M., Vlahović, S., Skorin-Kapov, L., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 0171 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This part addresses social acceptability and ecological validity in VR QoE testing. It outlines experimental designs (within/between-subjects), task typologies, environmental controls, and procedures for documenting context factors (public/private use, co-presence) that influence user judgments.

items.ti: Editorial: User states in extended reality media experiences for entertainment games
items.a: Lopes, P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Garcia, J., & Melhart, D.
items.v: Front. Virtual Real. 4:1235004
items.ab: This editorial introduces the research topic on user states in XR for games, outlining current challenges in measuring emotion, engagement, presence, and cybersickness across VR/AR platforms. It summarizes the featured contributions and highlights methodological advances and open problems for real-time, user-adaptive interactive systems.

items.ti: Shaping the Metaverse: policy engagement with immersive technologies in the UK
items.a: McWilliams, G., Phillips, D., McEvoy, B., Phillips, E., Lydon, D., Chang, J.-R., Martinez-del-Rincon, J., Quinn, W., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Harrington, C., Lee, L. H., Crooks, N., Alcorn, M. & Johnson, C.
items.v: Report for the UK Department for Culture, Media & Sport, commissioned through UKRI under the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme. Queen's University Belfast
items.ab: This paper summarizes UK policy dialogues on immersive technologies, spanning safety, privacy, accessibility, and economic opportunity. Drawing on workshops with industry, academia, and civil society, we identify priority areas for regulation and public service adoption. The work outlines actionable pathways for responsible metaverse development and cross-sector collaboration.

items.ti: Exploring users' sense of safety in public using an Augmented Reality application
items.a: Vergari, M., Kojic, T., Bertges, N., Vona, F., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 15th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2023), Ghent, Belgium
items.ab: We present an AR application for in-situ assessment of perceived safety in public spaces. In a field study, users annotated locations while the app captured contextual cues (e.g., lighting, crowding, visibility). Analyses reveal how AR prompts shape attention and reporting behavior, and identify environmental factors linked to safety perceptions. We discuss design implications for urban planning and wayfinding.

items.ti: Protect and Extend - Using GANs for Synthetic Data Generation of Time-Series Medical Records
items.a: Ashrafi, N., Schmitt, V., Spang, R. P., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 15th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2023), Ghent, Belgium
items.n: Diversity and Societal Impact Award, QoMEX 2023
items.ab: We introduce a GAN-based pipeline for generating realistic, privacy-preserving medical time-series to support model development when access to sensitive data is limited. Using fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics, we demonstrate that synthetic records can retain clinically meaningful patterns while mitigating re-identification risk. We discuss deployment considerations and ethical safeguards.

items.ti: An Investigation of the Influence of Ambient Noise on User Experience in Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojic, T., Vergari, M., Vona, F., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 15th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2023), Ghent, Belgium
items.ab: We examine how ambient noise conditions affect presence, performance, workload, and cybersickness during VR tasks. Comparing quiet, moderate, and noisy soundscapes with and without spatialized audio, we find that noise degrades immersion and increases effort, while appropriate audio design mitigates some negative effects. The results inform audio strategies for VR use in real-world environments.

items.ti: Embedding Self-Assessment Manikins in Mobile Augmented Reality Applications
items.a: Kojić, T., Luebbing, L., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (HCII 2023). Copenhagen, Denmark
items.ab: This paper explores integrating Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM) ratings directly into AR scenes on mobile devices. We compare spatial placements, scale, anchoring, and occlusion handling for rapid in-situ affect reporting during interaction. Results show that world-anchored, minimally occlusive SAM widgets reduce response time and cognitive load while preserving rating reliability, yielding practical UI patterns for emotion capture in AR.

items.ti: Designing User-Centered Simulations of Leadership Situations for Cave Automatic Virtual Environments: Development and Usability Study
items.a: Vona, F., Ceranic, M., Rybnikova, I., & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (HCII 2023). Copenhagen, Denmark
items.ab: We present the design and validation of immersive simulations for leadership training in a CAVE environment. Following a user-centered process with interviews, scenario co-creation, and iterative prototyping, we implemented branching social situations and multimodal feedback. A formative usability study (think-aloud, SUS, presence and workload ratings) indicates high acceptance, strong perceived realism, and clear design guidelines for balancing authenticity with simulator comfort.

items.ti: Effects of User Factors on User Experience in Virtual Reality - Age, Gender, and VR Experience as Influencing Factors for VR Exergames
items.a: Kojić, T., Spang. R. P., Vergari, M., Meier, L., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Quality and User Experience. 8, 3
items.ab: This study investigates how age, gender, and prior VR experience influence user experience in VR-based exergames. Results show significant differences in engagement, usability, and comfort, underscoring the need for inclusive design to ensure accessibility and enjoyment for diverse user groups.

items.ti: Smartphone Global Positioning System–Based System to Assess Mobility in Health Research: Development, Accuracy, and Usability Study
items.a: Spang. R. P., Haeger, C., Mümken, S.A., Brauer, M., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Gellert, P.
items.v: JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies. 10:e42258
items.ab: This paper presents the development and validation of a smartphone GPS-based system for assessing mobility in health research. Accuracy tests and usability evaluations indicate that the system provides reliable mobility data and is well-accepted by older adult participants.

items.ti: Impact of spatial auditory navigation on user experience during augmented outdoor navigation tasks
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Sun, Z., Vergari, M., Ashrafi, N., Vona, F., & Kojić, T.
items.v: Paper presented at the annual congress of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Akustik (DAGA 2023), Hamburg, Germany
items.ab: We evaluate spatialized audio cues for AR-supported outdoor navigation compared to non-spatial audio and visual-only guidance. Field trials assess route efficiency, situational awareness, workload, and perceived safety. Spatial audio improves turn compliance and reduces visual dependency without increasing distraction, supporting hybrid cue designs for hands-free navigation in real environments.

items.ti: Real-time affect detection in virtual reality: a technique based on a three-dimensional model of affect and EEG signals
items.a: Pinilla, A., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Garcia, J. A., Raffe, W. & Möller, S.
items.v: Front. Virtual Real. 3:964754
items.ab: This article introduces a method for detecting affective states in real time within virtual reality environments. Combining EEG signals with a three-dimensional model of affect, the study demonstrates the feasibility of emotion recognition to enhance adaptive VR systems.

items.ti: Dementia and the role of evidence-based guidelines in primary care – Results of a cluster randomised controlled trial
items.a: Lech, S., O´Sullivan, J. L., Spang, R. P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Gellert, P. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Paper presented at the GSA Annual Scientific Meeting
items.ab: This presentation reports primary care outcomes from a cluster-randomized trial evaluating adherence to dementia care guidelines. We analyze documentation quality, referral patterns, and patient-reported outcomes under guideline-oriented support versus usual care. Findings suggest that structured guideline implementation improves key process measures and may facilitate earlier interventions along the care pathway.

items.ti: ColorTable: Manipulating Tasting Experiences, Impact of Light Color on Food Flavor Perception
items.a: Burkert, P., Schaufler, B. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (HCII 2022). Virtual event
items.ab: ColorTable is an interactive setup that modulates table lighting to study crossmodal effects on flavor perception. In controlled tastings, we vary ambient light hues and intensities during food consumption and collect hedonic and sensory ratings. Results show systematic shifts in perceived sweetness and freshness, highlighting design opportunities for experiential dining and assistive nutrition contexts.

items.ti: The Storytime Dataset: Simulated Videotelephony Clips for Quality Perception Research
items.a: Spang, R. P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 14th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2022), Lippstadt, Germany
items.ab: We release Storytime, a dataset of controlled videotelephony clips with scripted conversational content and systematically varied network and encoding conditions. The corpus is designed for Quality of Experience studies, enabling reproducible analysis of perceived quality, attention, and affect. We describe generation procedures, annotations, and baseline results to facilitate benchmarking.

items.ti: Investigation of Personal Space perception in Augmented Reality
items.a: Vergari, M., Spang, R. P., Kojić, T., Hesse, B., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 14th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2022), Lippstadt, Germany
items.ab: We study proxemics in AR by measuring comfort boundaries when virtual characters and objects approach users in different trajectories and speeds. Results show asymmetries in tolerated distances and highlight how occlusion and spatial anchoring influence perceived intrusiveness. The findings inform placement rules for AR content that respects users’ personal space.

items.ti: Individual Technology-supported Mobility Support for People aged 75 and over in Rural Areas
items.a: Mümken, S., Haeger, C., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Spang, R. P. & Gellert, P.
items.v: Zeitschrift für Gerontologie und Geriatrie, 55(Suppl. 1), 110
items.ab_absent: Congress abstract in a supplement volume of Zeitschrift für Gerontologie und Geriatrie. Neither an abstract nor a DOI of its own exists — the supplement carries the identifier, not the individual contribution. Recorded so this reads as a fact rather than a gap still to be filled.

items.ti: Making Sense of the Noise - Integrating Multiple Analyses for Stop and Trip Classification
items.a: Spang, R. P., Pieper, K., Oesterle, B., Brauer, M., Haeger, C., Mümken, S., Gellert, P. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the Free and Open Source Software for Geospatial (FOSS4G 2022). Firenze, Italy
items.ab: We propose a robust pipeline for classifying stops and trips from noisy real-world GPS and accelerometer data. By combining density-based clustering, temporal smoothing, and sensor-fusion heuristics, the approach improves segmentation stability across heterogeneous devices and sampling rates. Open-source tools and benchmarks on daily-life datasets demonstrate higher precision/recall and practical defaults for mobility research.

items.ti: The STAGA-Dataset: Stop and Trip Annotated GPS and Accelerometer Data of Everyday Life
items.a: Spang, R. P., Pieper, K., Oesterle, B., Brauer, M., Haeger, C., Mümken, S., Gellert, P. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the Free and Open Source Software for Geospatial (FOSS4G 2022). Firenze, Italy
items.ab: We introduce STAGA, a curated dataset of everyday mobility with synchronized GPS and accelerometer streams and expert annotations for stops and trips. The corpus covers diverse contexts, devices, and sampling regimes to support method development and benchmarking. We describe collection, labeling protocols, and baseline models, and provide open access for reproducible mobility analytics.

items.ti: Reconstruction and Physiological Basis of Samsung’s Galaxy Watch Stress Score
items.a: Spang, R. P., Machačík, P., Pieper, K., Vergari, M. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Virtual event
items.ab: We reverse-engineer a commercial smartwatch stress metric by relating device outputs to concurrently recorded physiological signals. Using controlled tasks and free-living data, we examine contributions from HRV features and movement artifacts and compare against validated stress scales. The analysis clarifies construct coverage and limitations, offering guidance for research use of consumer stress indicators.

items.ti: Using Eye Tracking for Assessing User Experience of Text Readability in Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojić, T., Vergari, M., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Virtual event
items.ab: Virtual Reality (VR) technology is mostly used in gaming, videos, engineering applications, and training simulators. One thing which is shared among all of them is the necessity to display text. Text reading experience is not always in focus for VR systems because of limited hardware capabilities, lack of standardization, user interface (UI) design flaws, and physical design of Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs). With this paper, key variables from the UI design side were researched that can improve text reading user experience in VR. Therefore four important points for reading in VR application were selected to be focused on: 1) Difference in canvas type (flat/curved), 2) Contrast on virtual scene (light/dark), 3) Number of columns in layout (1 column/2 column/3 column) 4) Text distance from the subject (1.5 m/6.5 m). For a user study a VR app for Oculus Quest was developed, enabling the possibility to display text while varying some of the features important for readability in VR. This user experiment has shown parameters that are important for text reading experience in VR. Specifically, subjects performed very well when the text was on a 6.5-meter distance from the subject with font size 22pt, on a flat canvas with one column layout. When it comes to physiological variables, the conditions measurements were behaving similarly, as all of the selected parameters were in line with the design guidelines. Therefore, selection on final settings should be more oriented towards user experience and preferences.

items.ti: Towards Improvement of UX using Gamification for Public Artistic and Historical Artefacts in AR
items.a: Vergari, M., Kojić, T., Hillmann, S., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Virtual event
items.ab: We investigate game mechanics to enhance engagement with public art and heritage objects through mobile AR. A comparative field study tests points, quests, and cooperative tasks against a non-gamified baseline while tracking dwell time, learning, and social acceptability. Gamification increases exploration and recall without undermining site etiquette, suggesting design levers for cultural AR experiences.

items.ti: ITU-T P.IntVR: "Subjective Test Method for Interactive Virtual Reality Applications" - Quality of Experience aspects for Interactive Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 0060 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: We define a taxonomy of VR QoE aspects—presence, usability, comfort, cybersickness, aesthetics, task performance—and propose candidate scales and behavioral/physiological correlates. The document motivates harmonized metrics and reporting to enable cross-study comparability.

items.ti: Gestaltung Digitalisierung im Gesundheitswesen
items.a: Anstädt, T., Becker, K., Czaplik, M., Laurila-Dürsch, J., Friedrich, P., Hilfenhaus, C., Lingnau, B., Hübschen, M., Schmoldt, D., Strehlau, H., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Wolff, D.
items.v: VDE Positionspapier. Offenbach am Main: Informationstechnische Gesellschaft im VDE (ITG) mit Unterstützung der VDE DGBMT
items.ab: Das deutsche Gesundheitswesen krankt an akutem Fachkräftemangel. Schon seit Jahren macht die Bundesagentur für Arbeit auf die Schwierigkeit aufmerksam, Pflegestellen neu zu besetzen: Auf 100 Angebote kommen nur 35 Bewerber*innen. Vakanzzeiten von bis zu vier Monaten sind keine Seltenheit. Bereits heute fehlen über 50.000 Ärzt*innen und bald dreimal so viele nicht-ärztliche Fachkräfte. Diese Personallücke wird sich bis 2030 sogar auf fast eine Million Personen – gut 165.000 Ärzt*innen sowie fast 800.000 nicht-ärztliche Fachkräfte – vergrößern. In den stationären Einrichtungen dürfte etwa jede dritte Arztstelle unbesetzt bleiben, im ambulanten Bereich sogar jede zweite (PwC). In 2020 mussten etwa 61 Arbeitstage (1,3% mehr als 2019) pro Jahr und Praxis für die Erfüllung von Informationspflichten aufgewendet werden, so der Bürokratieindex BIX. Der digitale Wandel im Gesundheitswesen bietet für Deutschland großes Potenzial. So könnten beispielsweise elektronische Patientenakten, Telemedizin, elektronische Rezepte und automatisierte Erstattungen hohe Effizienzsteigerungen und Kosteneinsparungen bringen (OECD, 2020). Eine erfolgreiche digitale Transformation ist nicht nur eine technologische Angelegenheit, sondern erfordert einen komplexen angepassten Wandel der fachlichen Kompetenzen und Fähigkeiten. Gesundheitsarbeiter*innen berichten oft von mangelnden Gelegenheiten, um sich für die digitalen Werkzeuge und Systeme zu qualifizieren und diese vollumfänglich wie auch souverän zu nutzen. Es ist daher von Nöten, bedarfsgerechtere Berufsbilder zu schaffen und Weiter- oder Fortbildungsmaßnahmen zu überdenken, die sowohl technische als auch weiter gefasste Kompetenzen umfassen und nicht zwangsläufig Kenntnisse im Gesundheitsbereich voraussetzen. Um diesen Ansprüchen gerecht zu werden, werden Personen mit einer geeigneten beruflichen Qualifikation im Fachgebiet Digitalisierung im Gesundheitswesen in einem spezifischen Teilgebiet als Digital-technische Assistent*innen (DTA) weitergebildet bzw. Personen mit einer geeigneten beruflichen Qualifikation zur Ausübung des jeweiligen Fachgebiets oder eines Teilgebiets als Digital-technische Fachangestellte (DTFA) mit serviceorientierter Kompetenz oder anwendungsspezifischer Kompetenz in einem spezifischen Teilgebiet fortgebildet, um bereits bestehende Belastungen wie auch dem hinzukommenden digitalen Wandel im Gesundheitswesen entgegenzukommen. Weiter- oder fortgebildete DTA bzw. DTFA würden hier bereits für Entlastung sorgen, ebenso in Pflege- und Krankenhauseinrichtungen. Nach einem Gutachten von Roland Berger ließe sich somit sowohl medizinisches Personal wie auch Gesundheitspflegefachpersonal deutlich entlasten, wenn u.a. Patientenkoordinatoren administrative Aufgaben in Krankenhäusern übernehmen und sich um die gesamten Prozesse rund um die Patient*innen kümmern könnten. Auch hier wird die Bedeutung der Digital-technischen Assistent*in bzw. der Digital-technischen Fachangestellten erneut deutlich. Von der Patientenaufnahme über die Diagnostik, Operationsplanung bis hin zur Patientenentlassung können die Arbeitsbereiche der bedarfsgerechteren Berufsbilder aussehen. „Krankenhauspatienten bekämen so eine Rundumbetreuung aus allein einer Hand. Dies würde die Abwicklung von bürokratischen Verfahren deutlich beschleunigen und alle Betroffenen entlasten – zugunsten der Patientenbetreuung“, siehe nahfolgendes Fallbeispiel. Darüber hinaus bringen die DTA bzw. DTFA einen positiven Effekt hinsichtlich des zukünftigen Nachwuchses gesundheitlicher wie auch medizinischer Fachkräfte mit sich: Würden Ärzt*innen und Pflegepersonal sowohl vom bürokratischen Aufwand als auch von dem hohen Überstundenpensum durch DTA bzw. DTFA befreit werden, so ließen sich diese Berufe für medizinische wie auch pflegerische Absolventen wieder sehr viel attraktiver gestalten.

items.ti: Mobility enhancement among older adults 75 + in rural areas: Study protocol of the MOBILE randomized controlled trial
items.a: Haeger, C., Mümken, S.A., O‘Sullivan, J.L., Spang, R.P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Stockburger, M., Dräger, D. & Gellert, P.
items.v: BMC Geriatr 22, 65
items.ab: This protocol describes MOBILE, a randomized controlled trial aiming to improve out-of-home mobility among adults aged 75+ living in rural areas. The intervention combines individualized counseling with digital monitoring (e.g., GPS-based mobility measures) and evaluates effects on mobility behavior, quality of life, and health-related outcomes.

items.ti: A tablet-based intervention for activating nursing home residents with dementia: results from a cluster-randomized controlled trial
items.a: O'Sullivan, J. L., Lech, S., Gellert, P., Grittner, U., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Möller, S., Kuhlmey, A., & Nordheim, J.
items.v: International psychogeriatrics, 34(2), 129–141
items.ab: This cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluated the use of a tablet-based intervention to activate nursing home residents with dementia. Results indicate positive effects on resident engagement and activity levels, suggesting that digital interventions can support psychosocial care in dementia settings.

items.ti: Dementia care and the role of guideline adherence in primary care: cross-sectional findings from the DemTab study
items.a: Lech, S., O’Sullivan, J.L., Drewelies, J., Herrmann, W., Spang, R., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Nordheim, J., & Gellert, P.
items.v: BMC Geriatr, 21, 717
items.ab: This cross-sectional study examined guideline adherence in dementia care within primary care practices as part of the DemTab project. The findings reveal gaps in adherence, particularly in diagnostics and care planning, underscoring the need for improved implementation strategies.

items.ti: Working with environmental noise and noise-cancellation: A workload assessment with EEG and subjective measures
items.a: Pieper, K., Spang, R. P., Prietz, P., Möller, S., Paajanen, E., Vaalgamaa, M. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Front. Neurosci. 15:771533
items.ab: This study assessed the cognitive workload associated with environmental noise and the use of noise-cancellation technologies. Combining EEG data with subjective measures, the research provides insights into how auditory environments affect attention and performance.

items.ti: Nutzung GPS-basierter Bewegungsdaten im Längsschnitt zur Evaluation am Beispiel der MOBILE-Intervention zur Förderung außerhäuslicher Mobilität alter Menschen
items.a: Mümken, S., Spang, R. P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Ackermann, C., Dräger, D. & Gellert, P.
items.v: Paper presented at 20. Deutschen Kongress für Versorgungsforschung (20. DKVF DIGITAL). Weimar, Germany, online
items.ab: We demonstrate how longitudinal, passively collected GPS traces can be used to evaluate an intervention aiming to increase out-of-home mobility among older adults. From raw trajectories we derive interpretable indicators (e.g., time spent out of home, trip frequency, visited-area diversity) and assess their sensitivity to change over time. The approach proves feasible and privacy-preserving, and it complements survey-based outcomes with objective mobility behavior.

items.ti: ITU-T P.IntVR: "Subjective Test Method for Interactive Virtual Reality Applications"
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 602 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This initial proposal frames the scope and structure of a new recommendation for subjective evaluation of interactive VR. It summarizes use cases, identifies key QoE dimensions, and sketches methodological building blocks to be elaborated in subsequent contributions.

items.ti: Update of Human IF for ITU-T Rec G.1035
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 605 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: We propose updates to the human interface factors section of G.1035 to reflect modern interactive media and XR use cases. Revisions include user task models, perceptual constraints, and guidance on capturing user-centric performance and comfort indicators under variable network conditions.

items.ti: Emotion visualization in Virtual Reality: An integrative review
items.a: Pinilla, A., Garcia, J. A., Raffe, W., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Spang, R. & Möller, S.
items.v: Front. Virtual Real. 2:630731
items.ab: This integrative review examines approaches to visualizing emotions in virtual reality. The paper synthesizes findings across disciplines, highlighting methods, applications, and challenges in leveraging emotion visualization to enrich VR experiences.

items.ti: Influence of Visualisation Design of Data Streams on User Experience in Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojić, T., Vergari, M., Thangaraj, R., Braune, M. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Washington DC, USA
items.ab: We investigate how alternative VR visualization designs for continuous data streams affect comprehension, workload, and presence. Through a controlled study, we compare spatial placement (egocentric vs. exocentric), encoding (shape/size/animation), and temporal buffering on monitoring tasks. Results reveal trade-offs between immersion and readability and yield practical guidelines for instrument panels in analytic and training scenarios.

items.ti: Automatic Recognition of Experienced Emotional State from Body Movement
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Devaikin, P. & Kojić, T.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Washington DC, USA
items.ab: This work examines whether emotions experienced during interaction can be inferred from whole-body kinematics. Using pose and velocity features captured from motion sensors, we train classifiers to distinguish arousal and valence states validated by self-reports. The models reach robust performance across tasks, indicating the potential of movement-based affect sensing for interactive systems and XR experiences.

items.ti: DemSelf, a Mobile App for Self-Administered Touch-Based Cognitive Screening: Participatory Design with Stakeholders
items.a: Burghart, M., O´Sullivan, J. L., Spang, R. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Washington DC, USA
items.ab: We report a participatory design process for DemSelf, a mobile app supporting self-administered touch-based cognitive screening. Patients, caregivers, and clinicians co-created task flows, feedback, and accessibility features through workshops and iterative prototyping. Usability testing indicates high acceptance and clear requirements for guidance, transparency, and follow-up in self-screening contexts.

items.ti: User Experience of Connected Services in Cars
items.a: Ganser, K., Kojić, T. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction. Washington DC, USA
items.ab: We evaluate UX factors of in-vehicle connected services such as navigation, media, and telematics. Through scenario-based driving simulations and surveys, we analyze perceived usefulness, trust, workload, and distraction for different interaction modalities. Findings highlight the importance of reliability, glanceable UI, and progressive disclosure, leading to design recommendations for safer connected experiences.

items.ti: Implementation and Effects of an Information Technology-Based Intervention to Support Speech and Language Therapy Among Stroke Patients with Aphasia: Protocol for a Virtual Randomized Controlled Trial, JMIR Research Protoc. 2021;10(7):e30621,
items.a: Kim, E., Laird, L., Wilson, C., Bieg, T., Mildner, P., Möller, S., Schatz, R., Schwarz, S., Spang, R., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Rochon, E.
items.v: JMIR Research Protocols, 10(7):e30621
items.ab: This protocol details a virtual randomized controlled trial evaluating a mobile IT-supported intervention for naming rehabilitation in post-stroke aphasia. It outlines remote recruitment, tele-assessment, adherence monitoring, and primary outcomes on language performance, aiming to demonstrate feasibility and clinical benefit in a fully virtual design.

items.ti: Don’t Worry be Happy - Using virtual environments to induce emotional states measured by subjective scales and heart rate parameters
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Spang, R., Kojić, T., Meier, L., Vergari, M. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces (IEEE VR 2021), Lisbon, Portugal
items.ab: We examine whether tailored virtual environments can reliably induce distinct emotional states and how these states manifest in both subjective ratings and cardiac measures. Participants experienced calming, positive, and mildly stressful VR scenes while we recorded self-reports (valence/arousal scales) and heart-rate–derived metrics. Results show consistent shifts in affect with scene type and meaningful correlations between subjective arousal and heart-rate parameters, supporting VR as a controllable stimulus for affective research and training.

items.ti: Influence of Interactivity and Social Environments on User Experience and Social Acceptability in Virtual Reality
items.a: Vergari, M., Kojić, T., Vona, F., Garzotto, F., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces (IEEE VR 2021), Lisbon, Portugal
items.n: Conference Paper Honorable Mention, IEEE VR 2021
items.ab: This study manipulates interaction richness (low vs. high interactivity) and social context (alone, co-present peers, public bystanders) to explore trade-offs between presence, enjoyment, performance, and perceived social acceptability in VR. High interactivity generally improved engagement and perceived competence but, in public contexts, increased self-consciousness and acceptability concerns. We derive design implications for calibrating interaction demands to situational norms and bystander expectations.

items.ti: Contribution to ITU-T Rec G.1035: Contribution for Human Influencing Factors - Static and Dynamic Human Factors
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 562 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: The contribution refines the treatment of human influencing factors in Rec. G.1035 by distinguishing static (e.g., demographics, abilities) from dynamic (e.g., fatigue, affect, adaptation) user characteristics. It proposes measurement and reporting guidance to better capture these factors’ impact on perceived quality and performance in contemporary interactive media scenarios.

items.ti: Proposal for new Work Item P.IntVR: Subjective Test Method for Interactive Virtual Reality Applications
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 548 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This proposal initiates a new ITU-T work item to standardize subjective evaluation methods for interactive virtual reality (VR) applications. It outlines the motivation, scope, and core Quality of Experience (QoE) dimensions, and sketches a modular framework covering task design, participant management, instrumentation, and reporting to ensure reproducible and comparable VR studies.

items.ti: Contribution to DKE/AK STD_1000.8.5: VDE-Anwendungsregel "Digitale Qualifizierung im Gesundheitsbereich – Grundlagen"
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Contribution presented to the DKE Deutsche Kommission Elektrotechnik, Elektronik Informationstechnik in DIN und VDE, Frankfurt am Main, Germany
items.ab: This contribution supports a VDE application guideline on foundational aspects of digital qualification in healthcare. It describes competency profiles, training formats, and evaluation criteria for digital tools and processes, emphasizing usability, data protection, and patient safety as cross-cutting requirements for successful adoption.

items.ti: User-Specific Touch Interfaces: A Viable Solution for an Aging Society?
items.a: Shahal, A., Spang, R., Minge, M., Trahms, C. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Behaviour & Information Technology
items.ab: This article explores the design and evaluation of user-specific touch interfaces as a response to challenges posed by aging populations. Results suggest that personalized interfaces can improve usability and accessibility for older adults, offering a promising path for inclusive technology design.

items.ti: Ambulante Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz in Berlin und Umgebung - Querschnittsdaten aus der DemTab-Studie
items.a: Lech, S., O’Sullivan, J. L., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Greinacher, R., Gellert, P., Kuhlmey, A. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Abstract presented at the 2. Charité-Versorgungsforschungskongress. Berlin, Germany
items.ab: We present cross-sectional findings on outpatient care for people with dementia in Berlin and surrounding areas derived from the DemTab project. Descriptive analyses cover guideline adherence, care coordination, and patient/caregiver needs. The results reveal improvement potential in documentation and networking and motivate digital support to strengthen primary care pathways.

items.ti: Towards an updated understanding of immersive multimedia experiences
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Kojić, T.
items.v: ACM SIGMM Records, 13(4), Article 7, (2021)
items.ab: This article revisits the concept of immersive multimedia experience, proposing refinements to existing definitions and dimensions such as presence, agency, embodiment, and social acceptability. It calls for integrative evaluation frameworks that combine user-reported, behavioral, and physiological indicators across XR systems.

items.ti: Exploring Visualisation for Financial Statements in Virtual Reality
items.a: Kojić, T., Ashipala, S., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 2020 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality (AIVR), Utrecht, Netherlands
items.ab: We prototype VR visualizations for balance sheets and income statements to test whether spatialized layouts and embodied interaction aid comprehension. In a within-subjects evaluation, VR supported pattern discovery and comparative reasoning, but dense scenes elevated cognitive load and errors without careful hierarchy and labeling. We provide guidelines for data density, interaction granularity, and viewpoint control when bringing financial analytics into immersive spaces.

items.ti: QUALINET White Paper on Definitions of Immersive Media Experience (IMEx). arXiv preprint arXiv:2007.07032
items.a: Perkis, A., Timmerer, C., Baraković, S., Husić, J. B., Bech, S., Bosse, S., ... , Voigt-Antons, J.-N., …
items.v: arXiv preprint arXiv:2007.07032
items.ab: The white paper proposes shared terminology and conceptual dimensions for Immersive Media Experience (IMEx), spanning technological factors, user states, and context. It consolidates community perspectives and offers recommendations for interoperable evaluation methods to advance research and standardization in immersive media.

items.ti: DemTab – Tabletgestützte ambulante Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz: Leitlinienbasierte Behandlungsplanung, individuelles Krankheitsmanagement und Vernetzung
items.a: O’Sullivan, J. L., Lech, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Greinacher, R., Gellert, P., Kuhlmey, A. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Abstract presented at the Online-Symposium des Fachausschuss „Alter und Technik“ der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Gerontologie und Geriatrie (DGGG) "COVID-19 als <Brennglas>: Was wir aus der Krise zum Thema Altern und Digitalisierung lernen können“, virtual event
items.ab: This contribution outlines DemTab, a tablet-based solution to assist guideline-oriented treatment planning, self-management, and communication in outpatient dementia care. We describe core modules, stakeholder involvement, and early feasibility feedback from primary care practices. Initial experiences suggest improved transparency and coordination, alongside requirements for training and data security.

items.ti: 12170: User-Centered Design of a Multimodal Training App for People with Aphasia
items.a: Schatz, R., Kim, E. S., Bieber, A.-M., Bieg, T., Greinacher, R., Laird, L., Mildner, P., Neureiter, K., Rochon, E., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Proposal accepted at the Annual Convention of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, San Diego, CA (Convention canceled)
items.ab: We outline a user-centered design program for a multimodal aphasia training app combining speech, gesture, and visual cues. Co-design with clinicians and persons with aphasia informed task selection, progression, and feedback strategies; formative tests assessed usability and accessibility. The proposed framework targets home-based practice and clinical integration, emphasizing adaptability and motivation.

items.ti: Estimation of the Quality of Experience During Video Streaming From Facial Expression and Gaze Direction
items.a: Porcu, S., Floris, A., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Atzori, L. & Möller, S.
items.v: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, vol. 17, no. 4, pp. 2702-2716
items.n: Best Journal Paper Award, IEEE Communications Society (MMTC) 2023
items.ab: This paper proposes methods for estimating Quality of Experience (QoE) in video streaming by analyzing users’ facial expressions and gaze direction. Experimental results demonstrate that these non-intrusive behavioral cues provide reliable indicators of perceived quality. The study contributes to the development of automatic QoE monitoring systems and received the IEEE ComSoc Multimedia Communications Technical Committee Best Journal Paper Award in 2023.

items.ti: Predicting tap locations on touch screens in the field using accelerometer and gyroscope sensor readings
items.a: Schmitt, E. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (pp. 1-10). Springer, Cham
items.ab: We propose a lightweight method to infer tap locations on smartphones from inertial sensor data alone. Models trained on accelerometer and gyroscope signals generalize across users and devices and enable input reconstruction in real-world settings. Potential applications include implicit error detection, accessibility aids, and interaction analytics without screen capture.

items.ti: Accuracy Assessment of ARKit 2Based Gaze Estimation
items.a: Greinacher, R. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (pp. 1–10). Springer, Cham
items.ab: This paper benchmarks the accuracy of ARKit 2’s camera-based gaze estimation for common interaction distances and lighting settings. We measure angular error, stability, and drift against a reference eye tracker and analyze implications for selection, reading, and attention-aware UI. The results provide practical thresholds and calibration advice for deploying gaze-enabled AR on commodity devices.

items.ti: Comparing emotional states induced by 360 videos via head-mounted display and computer screen
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Lehtonen, E., Palacios, A. & Ali, D.
items.v: Paper presented at the 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland
items.ab: We compare the affective impact of 360° video presented on a head-mounted display versus a desktop screen. Using standardized self-reports of valence/arousal and behavioral indicators, HMD viewing produced stronger arousal and presence while maintaining comparable valence trends; some participants reported mild discomfort with HMDs. The findings clarify modality effects for emotion induction protocols using omnidirectional video.

items.ti: Influence of Hand Tracking as a Way of Interaction in Virtual Reality on User Experience
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Kojić, T., Ali, D. & Möller, S.
items.v: 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland

items.ti: Assessing Differences in Flow State Induced by an Adaptive Music Learning Software
items.a: Haug, M., Camps, P., Umland, T. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland

items.ti: Impact of Tactile and Visual Feedback on Breathing Rhythm and User Experience in VR Exergaming
items.a: Greinacher, R., Kojić, T., Meier, L., Parameshappa, R., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland
items.ab: We investigate how adding vibrotactile cues and visual pacing signals to a VR exergame affects respiratory regularity and perceived exertion. Compared to baseline, multimodal feedback improved breathing synchronization with target rhythms, reduced workload, and increased enjoyment. Results support incorporating lightweight haptics and visual guidance to promote safer, more effective exertion in VR fitness.

items.ti: Development and Validation of Pictographic Scales for Rapid Assessment of Affective States in Virtual Reality
items.a: Krüger, C., Kojić, T., Meier, L., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland
items.ab: We introduce language-independent pictographic scales designed for quick, in-headset assessment of valence and arousal during VR experiences. Across multiple tasks, the scales showed good reliability and convergent validity against established self-report measures while reducing interruption time. The instruments enable dense sampling of affect without breaking immersion.

items.ti: User Experience of Reading in Virtual Reality — Finding Values for Text Distance, Size and Contrast
items.a: Kojić, T., Ali, D., Greinacher, R., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 12th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2020), Athlone, Ireland
items.ab: We explore readability and comfort for in-headset text by systematically varying viewing distance, character size, and contrast. User performance and subjective fatigue reveal robust regions where comprehension is high and strain is low, alongside configurations that degrade legibility. We summarize practical parameter ranges to guide UI typography in VR applications.

items.ti: DemTab – Tablet-basierte ambulante Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz: eine cluster-randomisierte kontrollierte Studie
items.a: O’Sullivan, J. L., Lech, S., Gellert, P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Greinacher, R., Möller, S. Kuhlmey, A. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Paper presented at the IfG Jahrestagung "Wohnen und Gesundheit im Alter", Vechta, Germany
items.ab: Der Beitrag skizziert Design und Zielsetzung einer cluster-randomisierten Studie zur tabletbasierten Unterstützung der ambulanten Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz. Beschrieben werden Interventionsmodule (leitlinienbasierte Behandlungsplanung, Symptommonitoring, Kommunikation) sowie Rekrutierung, Randomisierung und primäre/sekundäre Outcomes. Erste Erfahrungen aus der Implementierung deuten auf eine gute Machbarkeit und Akzeptanz bei Hausarztpraxen und Angehörigen hin.

items.ti: Quality of life in people with dementia living in nursing homes: validation of an eight-item version of the QUALIDEM for intensive longitudinal assessment
items.a: Junge, S., Gellert, P., O’Sullivan, J.L., Möller, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Kuhlmey, A. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Qual Life Res 29, 1721–1730
items.ab: This study validates a shortened eight-item version of the QUALIDEM instrument for assessing quality of life in people with dementia living in nursing homes. The instrument was tested for reliability and sensitivity in intensive longitudinal studies, showing strong potential for use in daily care practice and research.

items.ti: Impact of Constant Visual Biofeedback on User Experience in Virtual Reality Exergames
items.a: Kojić, T., Nugyen, L. T. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 1st International Workshop on Bridging the Gap between Semantics and Multimedia Processing (SeMP 2019) at the 21st IEEE International Symposium on Multimedia (ISM 2019), San Diego, USA
items.ab: We evaluate continuous on-screen biofeedback (e.g., performance and physiological indicators) in a VR exergame with respect to motivation, perceived competence, and attentional demand. While constant feedback boosted goal orientation and pace, dense overlays increased visual load for some users. We discuss adaptive feedback strategies that preserve motivation while minimizing distraction.

items.ti: Informations- und Kommunikationstechnologien in der Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz
items.a: O‘Sullivan, J., Nordheim, J., Lech, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Gellert, P., & Kuhlmey, A.
items.v: Vortrag auf der Fachtagung der Sektionen III und IV der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Gerontologie und Geriatrie, Berlin, DE
items.ab: Der Vortrag gibt einen Überblick über Potenziale und Herausforderungen digitaler Anwendungen in der Demenzversorgung. Anhand von Praxisbeispielen (Telekonsultation, Tablet-gestützte Selbstmanagement-Tools, digitale Leitlinienunterstützung) werden Nutzen, Akzeptanz, Datenschutzfragen und Implementierungsbedingungen diskutiert. Im Fokus stehen Anforderungen verschiedener Stakeholder und Implikationen für zukünftige Versorgungsmodelle.

items.ti: Exploring Diachronic Changes of Biomedical Knowledge using Distributed Concept Representations
items.a: Vashisth, G., Mikhailov, M., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Roller, R.
items.v: Paper presented at the 18th ACL Workshop on Biomedical Natural Language Processing (BioNLP 2019), Florence, Italy
items.ab: We train time-sliced word embeddings on biomedical corpora to track how concepts evolve across years. By aligning vector spaces, we quantify semantic drift and highlight case studies where terminology and associations shift (e.g., emerging therapies, reclassified diseases). The approach supports literature monitoring and hypothesis generation in fast-moving domains.

items.ti: Influence of Network Delay in Virtual Reality Multiplayer Exergames: Who is actually delayed?
items.a: Kojić, T., Schmidt, S., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the 11th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2019), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: We study the perceptual consequences of asymmetric latency in competitive VR exergaming. User reports and telemetry show that players often attribute inconsistencies to the opponent, not the network, and that avatar prediction can mask or amplify delay cues depending on movement type. We outline implications for fairness perception and synchronization strategies in social VR.

items.ti: Influence of UI Complexity and Positioning on User Experience During VR Exergames
items.a: Kojić, T., Sirotina, U., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 11th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2019), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: We investigate how on-screen HUD complexity and spatial placement affect comfort, performance, and enjoyment in VR exergames. In a controlled study varying information density and UI positioning (fixed vs. world-locked; central vs. peripheral), higher complexity increased perceived workload and motion-related discomfort, while peripheral, minimally intrusive overlays preserved immersion and task performance. We provide practical guidelines for balancing feedback richness with legibility and situational awareness during intense movement.

items.ti: Emotional Impact of Video Quality: Self-Assessment and Facial Expression Recognition
items.a: Porcu, S., Uhrig, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Möller, S. & Atzori, L.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2019), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: This work examines how degradations in video quality shape viewers’ emotional responses using both subjective ratings and automatic facial expression analysis. Across controlled impairment levels, lower quality increased negative affect and reduced engagement, with facial action units aligning with self-reported valence and arousal trends. Results highlight the value of combined self-report and vision-based signals for continuous QoE monitoring.

items.ti: Tablet-based Outpatient Care of People with Dementia: A Qualitative Feasibility Study
items.a: Lech, S., Supplieth J., O‘Sullivan, J. L., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Gellert, P., Kuhlmey, A. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Poster presented at the International Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics European Region Congress, Gothenburg, SWE
items.ab: We report qualitative findings on the feasibility of a tablet-assisted care concept for community-dwelling people with dementia. Interviews and focus groups with patients, caregivers, and providers highlight perceived benefits (structured planning, improved communication) and barriers (training needs, data protection, workload). The insights inform design requirements and a subsequent controlled evaluation.

items.ti: Finding critical features for predicting quality of life in tablet-based serious games for dementia
items.a: Cha, J.*, Voigt-Antons, J.-N.*, Trahms, C., O’Sullivan, J., Gellert, P., Kuhlmey, A., Möller, S. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Quality and User Experience, 1-13
items.ab: This article investigates which gameplay features in tablet-based serious games are most relevant for predicting the quality of life of people with dementia. Using machine learning and gameplay data, the study identifies critical indicators that can guide the design of effective digital interventions. *Shared first authorship.

items.ti: Questionnaires Embedded in Virtual Environments: Reliability and positioning of rating scales in Virtual Environments
items.a: Regal, G.*, Voigt-Antons, J.-N.*, Schmidt, S., Schrammel, J., Kojić, T., Tscheligi, M. & Möller, S.
items.v: Quality and User Experience, 1-13
items.ab: This paper examines the reliability of questionnaires embedded directly within virtual environments, focusing on the positioning and design of rating scales. Findings indicate that scale placement and interaction modality influence user responses, providing recommendations for designing valid in-VR evaluation methods. *Shared first authorship.

items.ti: Tablet-Based Outpatient Care for People With Dementia - The DemTab Study Protocol
items.a: Lech, S., O’Sullivan, J. L., Gellert, P., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Nordheim J.
items.ab: This article outlines the study protocol for the DemTab project, which investigates tablet-based outpatient care for people with dementia. The project aims to improve guideline-based treatment planning, individualized disease management, and communication among care providers using digital tools.

items.ti: P300 indicates context-dependent change in speech quality beyond phonological change
items.a: Uhrig, S., Mittag, G., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Journal of Neural Engineering
items.ab: This study demonstrates that the P300 component of event-related potentials can capture context-dependent changes in speech quality, extending beyond purely phonological variations. The findings highlight the relevance of neurophysiological measures for assessing subjective speech quality perception.

items.ti: Associations of Health App Use and Perceived Effectiveness in People with Cardiovascular Diseases and Diabetes – a Population-based Survey
items.a: Ernsting, C., Stühmann, L.M., Dombrowski, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Kuhlmey, A. & Gellert, P.
items.v: JMIR mHealth and uHealth, 7(3):e12179
items.ab: This population-based survey explored the prevalence of health app use among individuals with cardiovascular diseases and diabetes, and examined perceived effectiveness. Results show that while usage is relatively common, perceived benefits vary across subgroups, with implications for app design and patient engagement strategies.

items.ti: Neural correlates of speech quality dimensions analyzed using electroencephalography (EEG)
items.a: Uhrig, S., Mittag, G., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Journal of Neural Engineering, 16(3)
items.ab: This article analyzes neural correlates of distinct speech quality dimensions using EEG. Results show that specific EEG patterns correspond to perceptual dimensions such as clarity and naturalness, providing objective insights into subjective speech quality perception.

items.ti: Mapping attention during gameplay: assessment of behavioral and event-related potential (ERP) markers in an auditory Oddball task
items.a: Núñez Castellar, E. P., Antons, J.-N., Marinazzo, D. & Van Looy, J.
items.v: Psychophysiology, e13347
items.ab: This study investigates attentional processes during gameplay by combining behavioral measures and event-related potentials (ERPs) using an auditory Oddball paradigm. Results show how specific ERP markers, alongside task performance, can provide objective insights into attentional demands in gaming environments, offering a bridge between cognitive neuroscience and game research.

items.ti: Tablet-based outpatient care for people with dementia: Guideline-based treatment planning, personalized disease management and network-based care
items.a: Lech, S., O’Sullivan-Solte, J., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Gellert, P. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Poster presented at the 14th International Congress of the European Geriatric Medicine Society (EuGMS), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: This poster outlines a tablet-supported outpatient care pathway for dementia that integrates guideline prompts, personalized monitoring, and secure communication among providers. We describe the system architecture, planned outcome measures, and stakeholder feedback from early pilots. The approach aims to enhance coordination while maintaining usability for older patients and caregivers.

items.ti: Using Virtual Reality and Head-Mounted Displays to Increase Performance in Rowing Workouts
items.a: Arndt, S., Perkis, A. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 1st International Workshop on Multimedia Content Analysis in Sports, Seoul, Korea
items.ab: We present a VR training setup for indoor rowing that couples immersive river-course visuals with real-time effort feedback to enhance motivation and pacing. Compared to a conventional display, the HMD condition yielded longer time-on-task and improved stroke consistency without increasing perceived exertion. The findings suggest VR can support adherence and performance in endurance workouts when feedback and presence are carefully calibrated.

items.ti: Tabletgestützte ambulante Versorgung von Menschen mit Demenz
items.a: Lech, S., Nordheim, J., Gellert, P., O’Sullivan-Solte, J. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the Kongress der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Gerontologie und Geriatrie, Köln, Germany
items.ab: Vorgestellt wird ein digitales Versorgungskonzept zur Unterstützung von Hausarztpraxen, Betroffenen und Angehörigen. Die Präsentation beschreibt Funktionsumfang (Assessment, Verlaufsdokumentation, Aufklärung), Erfahrungen aus der Pilotierung sowie Anforderungen an Schulung und Datensicherheit. Erste Rückmeldungen zeigen hohe Relevanz und nennen konkrete Verbesserungsbedarfe für den Praxiseinsatz.

items.ti: „OurPuppet“ – Entwicklung einer Mensch-Technik-Interaktion für die Unterstützung informell Pflegender
items.a: Dimitrov, T., Kramps, O., Naroska, E., Bolten, T., Demmer, J., Ressel, C., Könen, S., Matthies, O., Habibi, A., Polzehl, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Matip, E.-M., Mertens, J. & Heutelbeck, D.
items.v: Paper presented at the 1st cluster conference „Future of Nursing Care“, Oldenburg, Germany
items.ab: This contribution introduces “OurPuppet,” a human–technology interaction concept designed to support informal caregivers in routine tasks and emotional engagement. The system combines tangible interaction with assistive prompts and remote supervision features to reduce cognitive load and promote adherence to care routines. Early formative evaluations with caregivers indicated high perceived usefulness and approachable interaction, informing next design iterations.

items.ti: Influence of Virtual Environments and Conversations on User Engagement During Multiplayer Exergames
items.a: Kojić, T., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Schmidt, S., Tetzlaff, L., Kortowski, B., Sirotina, U. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: We analyze how thematic scene design and in-game voice conversations shape engagement and competitiveness in multiplayer VR exergames. Richer environments and lightweight conversational cues increased social presence and persistence, but excessive chatter occasionally hampered coordination. We outline design balances between social facilitation and task focus to sustain enjoyable physical activity.

items.ti: User Experience of Web Browsing - The Relationship of Usability and Quality of Experience
items.a: Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Hoßfeld, T., Egger-Lampl, S., Schatz, R. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: This poster explores how classic usability attributes (e.g., efficiency, learnability) interact with network- and content-driven QoE factors during web browsing. Empirical evidence suggests that minor usability frictions can amplify perceived quality degradations under constrained networks, whereas clear information scent and responsive layouts mitigate them. We propose a joint measurement approach and discuss implications for cross-layer optimization.

items.ti: Dissociating Perceptual Quality Dimensions of Transmitted Speech Using Electroencephalography
items.a: Uhrig, S., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: We probe whether distinct speech quality dimensions (e.g., coloration, discontinuity) evoke separable neural signatures measurable with EEG. Using controlled degradations and oddball-style contrasts, we observe differential ERP patterns and scalp distributions aligned with listeners’ perceptual categorization. Findings support the feasibility of mapping component-wise speech quality to neurophysiological markers.

items.ti: Impact of Virtual Environments on Motivation and Engagement during Exergames
items.a: Schmidt, S., Ehrenbrink, P., Weiß, B., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Kojić, T., Möller, S. & Johnston, A.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: We compare minimalistic training spaces to rich, theme-based VR worlds to study how scene design influences motivation and sustained effort in exergames. Themed environments increased enjoyment and voluntary session length without compromising perceived exertion, particularly when environmental feedback was tied to player performance. Design recommendations are distilled for motivating long-term physical activity.

items.ti: Estimating Quality Ratings from Touch Interactions in Mobile Games
items.a: Trahms, C., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: This paper investigates whether implicit touch features (e.g., gesture speed, pressure variability, error corrections) predict users’ perceived quality in mobile games. Machine learning models trained on interaction logs achieved promising accuracy in estimating MOS without explicit questionnaires. The approach enables passive, fine-grained QoE monitoring in the wild.

items.ti: Effects of delay on perceived quality, behavior and oscillatory brain activity in dyadic telephone conversations
items.a: Uhrig, S., Michael, T., Möller, S., Keller, P. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: We study conversational latency in a controlled telephone setup to quantify its impact on perceived quality, dialogue dynamics, and EEG oscillations. Even modest one-way delays disrupted turn-taking and increased cognitive workload, reflected in lower quality ratings and changes in frontal theta/alpha activity. The results provide multi-modal evidence for stringent latency targets in voice services.

items.ti: Predicting personality traits from touchscreen based interactions
items.a: Küster, L., Trahms, C. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2018), Sardinia, Italy
items.ab: This study explores whether unobtrusive features from everyday touchscreen interactions can predict stable personality traits. Using gesture dynamics (e.g., tap timing, swipe kinematics) gathered from mobile tasks, we trained models that achieved meaningful correlations with Big Five dimensions. Results highlight both the promise and ethical considerations of behavior-based personality inference in mobile UX research.

items.ti: Exploring Attitudes of Healthcare Professionals towards ICT-based Interventions for Nursing Home Residents with Dementia: A Mixed-Methods Approach
items.a: O’Sullivan, J., Gellert, P., Hesse, H., Jordan, L.-M., Möller, S., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Nordheim J.
items.v: Contemporary Nurse, 54(1), 13-25
items.ab: This mixed-methods study examines healthcare professionals’ perceptions of ICT-based interventions for residents with dementia in nursing homes. Findings reveal both enthusiasm for the potential benefits of ICT and concerns about usability, training needs, and integration into everyday care routines. The study highlights barriers and opportunities for implementing digital tools in dementia care.

items.ti: BeST-App: Mobile Applikation eines Spiegeltherapie-Eigentrainings nach Schlaganfall
items.a: Schiller, C., Jettkowski, K., Voigt-Antons, J.-N. & Dohle, C.
items.v: Poster presented at the 25. Jahrestagung der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Neurorehabilitation e. V. (DGNR). Deutschen Gesellschaft für Neurorehabilitation (DGNR), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: The poster presents BeST-App, a mobile application enabling self-administered mirror therapy after stroke. The app guides patients through structured exercise modules with multimedia instructions and progress tracking designed for home use. Preliminary feedback from therapists and patients indicates good usability and potential to support continuity of care between clinical and home settings.

items.ti: Comparing standard assessment of cognitive and motor abilities with the performance measures of mobile-health apps
items.a: Yadav, M., Küster, L., Trahms, C. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the 9th Scientific Meeting of the International Society for Research on Internet Interventions (ISRII 2017), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: We compare traditional clinical tests of cognitive and motor function with task-derived performance indicators captured by mHealth applications. Correlation analyses suggest app-based metrics can approximate selected constructs while offering higher sampling frequency and ecological validity. The work outlines opportunities and limitations for integrating app telemetry into routine assessment.

items.ti: Tablet-based intervention for Nursing Home Residents with Dementia: A cluster RCT
items.a: Nordheim, J., O’Sullivan, J., Gellert, P., Arndt, S., Kuhlmey, A. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 21st World Congress of Gerontology and Geriatrics. International Association of Gerontological Societies (IAGG 2017), San Francisco, USA
items.ab: We present the protocol of a cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating a tablet-based psychosocial intervention for nursing home residents with dementia. Primary outcomes target quality of life and behavioral symptoms; secondary outcomes include staff burden and feasibility metrics. The study addresses implementation at ward level and explores moderators of intervention effectiveness.

items.ti: Information and Communications Technology in Dementia Care: Acceptance among Professional Caregivers
items.a: O'Sullivan, J., Nordheim, J., Jordan, L., Hesse, B., Möller, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 21st World Congress of Gerontology and Geriatrics. International Association of Gerontological Societies (IAGG 2017), San Francisco, USA
items.ab: This contribution examines attitudes of professional caregivers toward ICT solutions in dementia care. Survey and interview data capture perceived usefulness, ease of use, barriers to adoption, and organizational prerequisites. Results inform implementation strategies and highlight the need for training, workflow integration, and clear privacy safeguards.

items.ti: Towards prediction of user experience from touch interactions with mobile applications
items.a: Trahms, C., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the International Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (HCII), Vancouver, Canada
items.ab: This poster examines whether low-level touch features collected during regular app use can predict subjective user experience. By extracting temporal and spatial characteristics from taps and gestures, regression models explained variance in perceived usability and satisfaction without explicit questionnaires. Findings motivate passive UX sensing pipelines for large-scale field studies.

items.ti: Exploring diverse measures for evaluating QoE in the context of WebRTC
items.a: De Moor, K. Arndt, S., Ammar, D., Voigt-Antons, J.-N., Perkis, A. & Heegaard, P.
items.v: Poster presented at the 9th International Conference on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2017), Erfurt, Germany
items.ab: We present a multi-faceted framework for assessing WebRTC Quality of Experience by combining subjective ratings with objective indicators from network, media, and interaction layers. Case studies show that integrating conversational metrics and perceptual video measures improves diagnostic power beyond traditional QoS parameters. The work argues for cross-layer instrumentation in real-time communications testing.

items.ti: Perceptual references for independent dimensions of speech quality as measured by electroencephalography
items.a: Uhrig, S., Arndt, S., Möller, S. & Voigt-Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Quality and User Experience, 2(1), 1-10
items.ab: The article explores how independent dimensions of speech quality can be differentiated using electroencephalography (EEG). The results demonstrate that EEG can identify distinct perceptual references for various quality dimensions, supporting its potential as a reliable tool for assessing user experience in speech communication.

items.ti: Did you notice it? – How can we predict the subjective detection of video quality changes from eye movements?
items.a: Radun, J., Nuutinen, M., Antons, J.-N. & Arndt, S.
items.v: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 11, 37–47
items.ab: This research investigates whether eye-tracking data can be used to predict subjective detection of video quality degradations. The study finds that gaze behavior, including fixation duration and saccade patterns, correlates with the detection of quality changes, offering a promising method for objective quality assessment in audiovisual research.

items.ti: Psychophysiology-based QoE Assessment: A Survey
items.a: Engelke, U., Darcy, D. P., Mulliken, G. H., Bosse, S., Martini, M.G. Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Chan, K. Y., Ramzan, N. & Brunnström, K.
items.v: Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 11, 6-21
items.ab: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of psychophysiological methods applied to Quality of Experience (QoE) research. It reviews measures such as EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological arousal indicators, discussing their advantages, limitations, and applicability in multimedia quality assessment.

items.ti: Eine Tablet-gestützte psychosoziale Intervention zur Erhaltung der Lebensqualität von Pflegeheimbewohnern mit Demenz
items.a: O’Sullivan, J., Antons, J.-N., Jordan, L.-M., Nordheim, J., Möller, S. & Kuhlmey, A.
items.v: Erste Ergebnisse des Forschungsprojekts PflegeTab als Poster. Poster presented at the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Psychiatrie und Psychotherapie, Psychosomatik und Nervenheilkunde Kongress 2016 (DGPPN 2016), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: Das Poster beschreibt Zielsetzung, Inhalte und Evaluationsplan einer tabletgestützten psychosozialen Intervention in Pflegeheimen. Es werden Module zur Aktivierung, Kommunikation und Angehörigeneinbindung vorgestellt sowie erste Rückmeldungen von Pflegekräften zur Umsetzbarkeit zusammengefasst. Der Ansatz zielt auf niedrigschwellige, alltagsnahe Maßnahmen zur Lebensqualitätsförderung.

items.ti: Akzeptanz neuer Technologien im Arbeitsalltag von Pflegeheimmitarbeitern
items.a: O’Sullivan, J., Jordan, L.-M., Antons, J.-N., Gellert, P. & Nordheim, J.
items.v: Poster presented at the Gesundheit – bio.psycho.sozial 2.0 – Jahrestagung der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Medizinische Soziologie (DGMS) und der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Medizinische Psychologie (DGMP), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: Untersucht werden Akzeptanzfaktoren für digitale Lösungen im Pflegeheimalltag aus Sicht der Mitarbeitenden. Anhand einer Befragung werden Nutzenwahrnehmung, Bedienbarkeit, Belastung und organisationaler Support analysiert. Die Ergebnisse benennen zentrale Hürden und unterstützen die zielgerichtete Einführung technologiegestützter Prozesse in Pflegeeinrichtungen.

items.ti: Functional connectivity of orienting and executive attentional networks during flow: Granger Causality analysis of EEG recordings
items.a: Núñez Castellar, E. P., Antons, J.-N., Marinazzo, D. & Van Looy, J.
items.v: Paper presented at the 18th World Congress of the International Organization of Psychophysiology (IOP 2016), Habana, Cuba
items.ab: We analyze EEG recordings from gameplay to explore directed functional connectivity between orienting and executive attentional networks during self-reported flow. Using Granger causality, we compare connectivity patterns across low-, medium-, and high-engagement conditions. Findings support a reconfiguration toward more efficient information transfer under flow, offering neural evidence for attentional tuning in optimal experience.

items.ti: Enhancing Video Streaming Using Real-Time Gaze Tracking
items.a: Arndt, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 5th International Workshop on Perceptual Quality of Systems (PQS 2016), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: We propose a gaze-adaptive streaming approach that exploits real-time eye-tracking to prioritize foveated regions. Prototype evaluations show bandwidth savings while preserving perceived quality by allocating higher fidelity near gaze and reducing quality in peripheral areas. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating eye-tracking into QoE-aware streaming pipelines.

items.ti: User Experience in Authentication Research: A Survey
items.a: Kraus, L., Antons, J.-N., Kaiser, F. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 5th International Workshop on Perceptual Quality of Systems (PQS 2016), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: This survey reviews UX aspects of user authentication, covering memorability, effort, error tolerance, perceived security, and context of use across passwords, biometrics, and multi-factor methods. We synthesize empirical findings and highlight trade-offs between security and convenience. The paper outlines a research agenda for UX-centered authentication design and evaluation.

items.ti: Measuring flow through attentional engagement during game play: validation of a novel technique
items.a: Núñez Castellar, E. P., Antons, J.-N., Marinazzo, D. & Van Looy, J.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Communication Association Conference (ICA 2016), Fukuoka, Japan
items.ab: We introduce a method to index flow during gameplay by combining behavioral markers with attention-related measures. Across controlled difficulty manipulations, the proposed indices tracked transitions into and out of flow states and correlated with self-reports. The approach offers a practical, temporally sensitive tool for evaluating game experiences.

items.ti: PflegeTab: Enhancing Quality of Life Using a Psychosocial Internet-based Intervention for Residential Dementia Care
items.a: Antons, J.-N., O’Sullivan, J., Arndt, S., Gellert, P., Nordheim, J., Möller, S. & Kuhlmey, A.
items.v: Poster presented at the 8th Scientific Meeting of the International Society for Research on Internet Interventions (ISRII 2016), Seattle, USA
items.ab: PflegeTab is a tablet-supported psychosocial intervention co-designed with care staff to stimulate meaningful activities and communication for residents with dementia. The poster reports on feasibility, acceptance, and early indications of improved mood and engagement in nursing home settings. Lessons learned inform deployment and training strategies for technology-enabled dementia care.

items.ti: Using Electroencephalography to Analyze Sleepiness due to Low-quality Audiovisual Stimuli
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., & Möller, S.
items.v: Signal Processing: Image Communication, 42, 120-129
items.ab: The paper examines how exposure to low-quality audiovisual stimuli affects sleepiness, using EEG measurements to identify neural correlates. Results indicate that poor media quality increases drowsiness, suggesting important implications for user safety and media consumption contexts.

items.ti: Review on Using Physiology in Quality of Experience
items.a: Arndt, S., Brunnström, K., Cheng, E., Engelke, U., Möller, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Poster presented at the International Symposium on Human Vision and Electronic Imaging (HVEI 2016), San Francisco, USA
items.ab: We survey physiological methods—EEG, EDA, heart rate, respiration, eye movements—for assessing multimedia Quality of Experience. The review synthesizes study designs, signal processing pipelines, and validity considerations, and identifies scenarios where physiology complements or augments self-report. Recommendations are provided for multimodal QoE experiments and future standardization efforts.

items.ti: Structure proposal for the work item on the use of physiological measures as an additional test method for speech quality assessment (P.PHYSIO)
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S. & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 307 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: The document proposes a structure for a recommendation on integrating physiological measurements (e.g., EEG, EDA, heart rate) into speech quality assessment. It delineates use cases, experimental paradigms, candidate indicators, and data handling practices to complement subjective ratings with objective correlates of listener effort and affect.

items.ti: Motivating New Interaction Experiences Involving Implicit Interaction, Body Sensors, Adaptive, and Persuasive Interfaces
items.a: Möller, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the Future and Emerging Trends in Language Technology (FETLT 2015), Seville, Spain
items.ab: This contribution outlines a research agenda for next-generation human–computer interaction that leverages implicit inputs from body sensors alongside adaptive and persuasive interface concepts. We map key use cases in language technologies, discuss sensing and inference pipelines (from physiological data to intent), and highlight design and ethics challenges around transparency, privacy, and user agency.

items.ti: Investigating the Neural Correlates of the Subjective Flow Experience During Game Play: an EEG Study
items.a: Núñez Castellar, E. P., Antons, J.-N. & Van Looy, J.
items.v: Poster presented at the annual congress of the Organization for Human Brain Mapping (OHBM 2015), Honolulu, USA
items.ab: We report EEG evidence linking self-reported flow during gameplay to changes in oscillatory activity and event-related potentials. Participants played under manipulated challenge–skill balance; spectral and ERP markers were compared across conditions. Results suggest enhanced attentional engagement and more efficient processing during high-flow episodes, supporting neurocognitive accounts of optimal experience.

items.ti: Proposal to Work on a Recommendation on the Use of Physiological Measures as an Additional Test Method for Speech Quality Assessment
items.a: Möller, S., Antons, J.-N. & Arndt, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 - C 272 - E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This proposal motivates the development of a recommendation defining how physiological signals can augment traditional subjective speech quality tests. It reviews evidence linking physiology to perceived quality and outlines a roadmap covering instrumentation, protocols, and validation against established listening test outcomes.

items.ti: Comments on Draft P.GAME
items.a: Möller, S., Antons, J.-N., Beyer, J., Egger, S., Núñez Castellar, E. P., Skorin-Kapov, L. & Suznjevic, M.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 - C 270 - E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: The contribution provides technical and methodological comments on the draft recommendation P.GAME for gaming QoE assessment. It addresses stimulus design, session control, rating scales, and reporting to better capture interactivity, challenge, and engagement in both cloud and local gaming scenarios.

items.ti: Impact of Perceived Quality and other Influencing Factors on Emotional Video Experience
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S., De Moor, K. & Zander, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 7th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2015), Costa Navarino, Messinia, Greece
items.ab: We investigate how perceived audiovisual quality interacts with contextual and user-related factors to shape viewers’ emotional experience. Using controlled quality degradations and standardized affect self-reports, we show that quality drops reliably reduce positive affect and increase arousal, but the magnitude is moderated by content genre and individual sensitivity.
