The results highlight the need for QoE models that integrate technical, contextual, and human factors when predicting emotional impact.

items.ti: A method for feedback delay measurement using a low-cost Arduino microcontroller
items.a: Beyer, J., Varbelow, R., Antons, J.-N. & Zander, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 7th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2015), Costa Navarino, Messinia, Greece
items.ab: This work presents an inexpensive, reproducible setup based on an Arduino microcontroller to measure end-to-end feedback delays in interactive systems. We describe the hardware design, calibration procedure, and measurement accuracy, and validate the approach against reference instruments. The proposed method achieves millisecond resolution at a fraction of the cost, enabling broader adoption in QoE and HCI latency studies.

items.ti: Emotional Responses to Thermally Augmented Audiovisual Stimuli
items.a: Greiner, S., Antons, J.-N. & Wechsung, I.
items.v: Paper presented at the 7th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2015), Costa Navarino, Messinia, Greece
items.ab: We examine whether adding controlled thermal cues to audiovisual content modulates emotional responses. In a within-subjects experiment using affectively charged video clips, synchronized warm and cool stimuli intensified valence and arousal ratings and altered engagement without harming perceived quality. Findings suggest thermal augmentation as a promising channel for affective XR and multisensory media.

items.ti: Using electroencephalography and subjective self-assessment to measure the influence of quality variations in cloud gaming
items.a: Beyer, J., Varbelow, R., Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 7th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2015), Costa Navarino, Messinia, Greece
items.ab: This paper combines EEG markers with self-report to assess how network-induced quality degradations affect cloud gaming experiences. Packet loss and latency manipulations reduced reported enjoyment and elicited changes in oscillatory activity associated with increased workload and decreased engagement. The results demonstrate the added value of neurophysiological measures for diagnosing QoE impairments in interactive media.

items.ti: Towards a New ITU-T Recommendation for Subjective Methods Evaluating Gaming QoE
items.a: Möller, S., Antons, J.-N., Beyer, J., Egger, S., Núñez Castellar, E. P., Skorin-Kapov, L & Suznjevic, M.
items.v: Paper presented at the 7th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2015), Costa Navarino, Messinia, Greece
items.ab: We outline requirements and methodological building blocks for an ITU-T recommendation on subjective evaluation of gaming Quality of Experience. Drawing on existing standards and gaming-specific constructs (e.g., flow, presence, responsiveness), we propose test paradigms, task designs, and rating scales suitable for diverse game genres and platforms. The contribution aims to catalyze harmonized procedures for reproducible gaming QoE studies.

items.ti: Indirect assessment of subjective flow experience during game play: adaptation of an attentional behavioral paradigm
items.a: Núñez Castellar, E. P., Antons, J.-N., Vervaeke, J., de Ferrere, E. & Van Looy, J.
items.v: Paper presented at the International Communication Association Game Studies Preconference (ICA 2015), San Juan, Puerto Rico
items.ab: We adapt an attention-based behavioral paradigm to infer players’ flow states without interrupting gameplay. Performance on secondary probe tasks and response variability tracked self-reported flow across manipulated challenge levels, supporting the paradigm’s sensitivity. The approach enables continuous, minimally intrusive flow assessment suitable for laboratory and field studies.

items.ti: Challenging ITU-T P.835: Searching for the optimal order of scales for assessing the quality of complex speech signals
items.a: Arndt, S., Möller, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 41st annual congress of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Akustik (DAGA 2015), Nürnberg, Germany
items.ab: The study examines how the order of rating scales in P.835-style listening tests (speech, background noise, overall quality) influences judgments for complex, degraded speech. Using counterbalanced scale orders, we analyze order effects, response consistency, and test–retest reliability. Findings inform recommendations for robust protocol design in speech quality assessment.

items.ti: Neural Correlates of Quality Perception for Complex Speech Signals
items.a: Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Cham, Switzerland: Springer
items.ab: This book interconnects two essential disciplines to study the perception of speech: Neuroscience and Quality of Experience, which to date have rarely been used together for the purposes of research on speech quality perception. In five key experiments, the book demonstrates the application of standard clinical methods in neurophysiology on the one hand and of methods used in fields of research concerned with speech quality perception on the other. Using this combination, the book shows that speech stimuli with different lengths and different quality impairments are accompanied by physiological reactions related to quality variations, e.g., a positive peak in an event-related potential. Furthermore, it demonstrates that – in most cases – quality impairment intensity has an impact on the intensity of physiological reactions

items.ti: Effect of Presenting Multiple vs. Single Rating Scales After Stimulus Presentation on Subjective Quality Ratings
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S. & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 201 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This study examines whether administering multiple rating scales sequentially versus a single overall scale after stimulus presentation biases subjective quality judgments. Analyses of order and scale-count effects inform practical guidance for minimizing cognitive load and context effects in listening test protocols.

items.ti: Evaluation von automatisierter Erfassung der Blickzuwendung während der Spiegeltherapie
items.a: Hesse, B., Morkisch, N., Antons, J.-N. & Dohle, C.
items.v: Paper presented at the 5th Gemeinsamen Jahrestagung der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Neurorehabilitation (DGNR) und der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Neurotraumatologie und Klinische Neurorehabilitation (DGNKN). Deutsche Gesellschaft für Neurorehabilitation (DGNR), Singen, Germany
items.ab: Der Beitrag evaluiert ein automatisiertes Verfahren zur Erfassung der Blickzuwendung während der Spiegeltherapie nach Schlaganfall. Mittels kamerabasierter Blickdetektion werden Therapietreue und Aufmerksamkeitsfokussierung quantifiziert und mit klinischen Einschätzungen verglichen. Erste Ergebnisse belegen eine hohe Übereinstimmung und zeigen das Potenzial für objektive Prozessindikatoren in der Neurorehabilitation.

items.ti: Is Low Quality Media Affecting the Level of Fatigue?
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the 6th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2014), Singapore, Singapore
items.ab: We test whether exposure to low-quality audiovisual content increases viewer fatigue. Across controlled viewing sessions, degraded material elevated subjective tiredness and altered blink behavior relative to high-quality baselines. The findings suggest that long-term consumption of poor quality media can measurably tax attentional resources and comfort.

items.ti: Using Eye-Tracking and Correlates of Brain Activity to Predict Quality Scores
items.a: Arndt, S., Radun, J., Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the 6th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2014), Singapore, Singapore
items.ab: This poster evaluates whether objective measures—eye movements and EEG features—can predict subjective quality ratings of video. Models using fixation patterns and event-related activity explained significant variance in mean opinion scores, outperforming baselines relying on signal metrics alone. Results support multimodal user-centric prediction for QoE assessment.

items.ti: A Next Step Towards Measuring Perceived Quality of Speech Through Physiology
items.a: Arndt, S., Wenzel, M., Antons, J.-N., Köster, F., Möller, S. & Curio, Gabriel
items.v: Paper presented at the 15th Annual Conference of International Speech Communication Association (INTERSPEECH 2014), Singapore, Singapore
items.ab: We present physiological indices sensitive to perceived speech quality under controlled degradations. Combining EEG components with peripheral measures improved discrimination between codec and noise conditions compared to subjective ratings alone. The findings advance physiological measurement as a complementary tool for speech quality evaluation and standardization.

items.ti: Characterization of Human Emotions and Preferences for Text-to-Speech Systems Using Multimodal Neuroimaging Methods
items.a: Rehman Laghari, K., Gupta, R., Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Paper presented at the IEEE Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (CCECE 2014), Toronto, ON, Canada
items.ab: We investigate how listeners’ emotional responses and preferences to text-to-speech (TTS) voices can be quantified using a multimodal approach. Behavioral ratings are combined with EEG- and peripheral-physiology–based features while participants listen to TTS variants differing in prosody and signal quality. Results show reliable links between frontal EEG markers, arousal/valence reports, and user preference, suggesting neurophysiological measures as complementary indicators for TTS evaluation.

items.ti: Methods for Assessing the Quality of Transmitted Speech and of Speech Communication Services
items.a: Köster, F., Möller, S., Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S., Guse, D. & Weiss, B.
items.v: Acoustics Australia, 42, 179–184
items.ab: This article reviews different methods for evaluating transmitted speech and speech communication services. It compares subjective listening tests, instrumental measures, and hybrid approaches, emphasizing the importance of context-specific evaluation for improving communication quality.

items.ti: Using Electroencephalography to Measure Perceived Video Quality
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 8, 366–376
items.ab: This study explores how EEG can be used to assess perceived video quality. The findings suggest that neural signals can capture users’ sensitivity to quality variations, offering a promising complement to traditional subjective rating methods in multimedia evaluation.

items.ti: Brain Activity Correlates of Quality of Experience
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S., Schleicher, R. & Möller, S.
items.v: In S. Möller & A. Raake (Eds.), Quality of Experience (pp.109–120). Cham, Switzerland: Springer
items.ab: This chapter outlines common brain activity correlates that are known from neuroscience, gives an overview on established electrophysiological analysis methods and on the background of electroencephalography (EEG). After that an overview on study designs will be given and a practical guideline for the design of experiments using EEG in the research area of Quality of Experience (QoE) will be presented. At the end of this chapter we will close with a summary, give practical advice, and we will outline potential interesting future research topics.

items.ti: Evoking Emotions and Evaluating Emotional Impact
items.a: Schleicher, R. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: In S. Möller & A. Raake (Eds.), Quality of Experience (pp.121–132). Cham, Switzerland: Springer International Publishing
items.ab: This chapter gives an overview for Quality of Experience (QoE) practitioners on common setups in emotion research using audio (sounds), visual (pictures) and audiovisual (video clips) stimulus material to induce emotions. After presenting available databases for the different modalities, methods for subsequent as well as continuous self-assessment are discussed. Next to self-assessment, analysis of accompanying physiological changes is a common means to evaluate emotional responses. Here, typical measures of peripheral physiology are summarized. Finally, practical advices for including material with emotional content and recording physiological signals in experiments on audiovisual quality are given, and future research directions are outlined.

items.ti: Effects of Rating Scale Order on Subjective Quality Ratings of the Speech Signal Alone, the Background Noise Alone, and Overall Quality
items.a: Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 113 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: The contribution investigates how the order of speech-quality, noise-quality, and overall-quality scales affects listeners’ responses in complex speech scenarios. It reports systematic order effects and proposes recommended question sequences to improve reliability and interpretability of P.835-style evaluations.

items.ti: Using Physiological Data for Assessing Variations of the Cognitive State Evoked by Quality Profiles
items.a: Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 112 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: This document explores physiological correlates (e.g., EEG, EOG, HRV) as indicators of cognitive state changes induced by different quality profiles in audiovisual systems. It outlines candidate features, experimental designs, and validation strategies for integrating physiology into QoE assessment workflows.

items.ti: Objective Characterization of Human Behavioural Characteristics for QoE Assessment: A Pilot Study on the Use of Electroencephalography Features
items.a: Laghari, K., Gupta, R., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Paper presented at the Globecom 2013 Workshop - Quality of Experience for Multimedia Communications (QoEMC 2013), Atlanta, GA, USA
items.ab: This pilot study explores EEG-derived features as objective correlates of multimedia Quality of Experience (QoE). Under controlled degradations, we extract spectral and event-related EEG indicators and relate them to mean opinion scores and task performance. Findings indicate that specific EEG bands track perceived quality changes, supporting their use as supplementary, user-centric QoE metrics.

items.ti: The Effects of Text-to-Speech System Quality on Emotional States and Frontal Alpha Band Power
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Gupta, R., Laghari, K., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Paper presented at the 6th International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering, San Diego, CA, USA
items.ab: We examine how variations in TTS quality influence listeners’ affect and frontal alpha activity. Lower quality synthesis decreases pleasantness ratings and is associated with shifts in frontal alpha power indicative of altered attentional demands. The results provide converging behavioral and neurophysiological evidence that TTS quality modulates emotional experience and cognitive load.

items.ti: Einfluss der Audiomodalität auf die Wahrnehmung und Qualitätsbeurteilung (audio-)visueller Stimuli
items.a: Arndt, S., Bürglen, J., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R. & Möller, S.
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th Berliner Werkstatt Mensch-Maschine-Systeme, Berlin, Germany
items.ab: Der Beitrag untersucht, wie die verfügbare Audiomodalität die Wahrnehmung und Qualitätsurteile audiovisueller Inhalte beeinflusst. In einem faktoriellen Design variieren wir Tonpräsenz und -qualität sowie das Bildsignal und erfassen subjektive Ratings und Verhaltensmaße. Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Audio die Gesamtqualität überproportional prägt und Bildartefakte teilweise kompensieren kann, was Implikationen für QoE-Tests hat.

items.ti: Effect of Questionnaire Order on Ratings of Perceived Quality and Experienced Affect
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S. & Schleicher, R.
items.v: Paper presented at the 4th International Workshop on Perceptual Quality of Systems (PQS 2013), Vienna, Austria
items.ab: We test whether the order of administering quality and affect questionnaires biases reported outcomes in audiovisual QoE studies. Across counterbalanced sequences, presenting affect scales before overall quality yields systematically different ratings compared to the reverse order. The findings underscore the need for standardized, order-aware protocols to ensure comparability of subjective assessments.

items.ti: Does Low Quality Audiovisual Content Increase Fatigue of Viewers?
items.a: Arndt, S., Schleicher, R. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 4th International Workshop on Perceptual Quality of Systems (PQS 2013), Vienna, Austria
items.ab: This study evaluates viewer fatigue under prolonged exposure to degraded audiovisual material. Using self-reported tiredness, blink-rate metrics, and task performance, we find that lower content quality leads to increased fatigue compared to high-quality baselines. The results highlight fatigue as a relevant user-centric outcome for QoE evaluations.

items.ti: Changes in blinking behavior while watching videos with reduced quality
items.a: Schleicher, R., Arndt, S. & Antons, J.-N.
items.v: Paper presented at the 17th European Conference on Eye Movements (ECEM 2013), Lund, Sweden
items.ab: We analyze blink dynamics as a non-intrusive indicator of strain during viewing of degraded videos. Reduced quality conditions increase blink frequency and alter inter-blink intervals relative to high-quality content, consistent with heightened visual fatigue. The findings motivate the inclusion of blink measures in passive QoE monitoring.

items.ti: Subjective quality ratings and physiological correlates of synthesized speech
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Gupta, R., Laghari, K., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Poster presented at the 5th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2013), Klagenfurt, Austria
items.ab: We relate subjective quality judgments of synthesized speech to physiological measures collected during listening. Variations in synthesis parameters modulate both perceived quality and autonomic/EEG indicators, with moderate correlations between ratings and physiological responses. Results support multimodal assessment for a richer characterization of TTS QoE.

items.ti: Changes of vigilance caused by varying bit rate conditions
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Köster, F., Arndt, S., Möller, S. & Schleicher, R.
items.v: Poster presented at the 5th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2013), Klagenfurt, Austria
items.ab: This poster explores how bitrate-induced video quality variations affect viewer vigilance during extended sessions. Objective measures of alertness and subjective workload indicate decreased vigilance under low bitrate conditions compared to higher quality streams. The findings point to sustained attention costs associated with persistent quality impairments.

items.ti: Auditory BCIs for Visually Impaired Users: Should Developers Worry About the Quality of Text-to-Speech Readers?
items.a: Laghari, K., Gupta, R., Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Paper presented at the 5th International BCI Meeting, Pacific Grove, CA, USA
items.ab: We discuss the role of TTS quality in auditory brain–computer interface (BCI) design for visually impaired users. Through a small-scale evaluation, differences in TTS intelligibility and naturalness are shown to impact workload, accuracy, and user preference in auditory BCI tasks. We derive recommendations for selecting and tuning TTS to improve accessibility and performance.

items.ti: Neurophysiological Experimental Facility for Quality of Experience (QoE) Assessment
items.a: Laghari, K., Gupta, R., Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Paper presented at the 1st IFIP/IEEE international workshop on quality of experience (QoE) centric management (QCMan 2013), Ghent, Belgium
items.ab: This paper introduces an experimental facility specifically designed to study Quality of Experience (QoE) using neurophysiological measurements. The facility integrates multimodal data acquisition including EEG, physiological sensors, and behavioral logging, enabling comprehensive analysis of user states under controlled multimedia conditions. The setup provides a standardized platform to develop objective QoE metrics complementing traditional subjective approaches.

items.ti: Cognitive, Affective, and Experience Correlates of Speech Quality Perception in Complex Listening Conditions
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Laghari, K., Arndt, S., Schleicher, R., Möller, S., O’Shaughnessy, D. & Falk, T. H.
items.v: Poster presented at the IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP 2013), Vancouver, BC, Canada
items.ab: We investigate how speech quality perception in noisy and complex listening conditions relates to cognitive load, affective states, and experiential measures. Subjective ratings are complemented with EEG and peripheral physiological indicators to identify objective correlates of degraded speech signals. Results highlight distinct cognitive and emotional processing patterns associated with speech quality, offering insights for QoE assessment.

items.ti: Did You Notice? Neuronal Processing of Multimodal Mobile Phone Feedback
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S., Seebode, J., Schleicher, R. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the annual conference on Computer-Human Interaction (CHI 2013), Paris, France
items.ab: This poster explores the neuronal processing of multimodal feedback cues (haptic, auditory, visual) in mobile phone interaction. EEG and behavioral measures are employed to determine whether users consciously perceive subtle feedback events. Findings suggest that certain feedback modalities elicit detectable neural responses even when users are unaware, providing implications for the design of intuitive mobile interfaces.

items.ti: Investigating the Subjective Judgment Process Using Physiological Data
items.a: Antons, J.-N. & Möller, S.
items.v: Contribution presented to the ITU-T SG12 as COM 12 – C 39 – E, Geneva, Switzerland
items.ab: The contribution proposes leveraging physiological measurements to probe the temporal dynamics of subjective quality judgment. It discusses hypotheses linking attentional engagement and workload to rating behavior, suggesting multimodal experimental setups to relate physiological markers to moment-by-moment decision processes.

items.ti: Neural correlates of Affective States and Speech Perception: Towards Quality-of- Experience Measurement of Reverberant Speech
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Laghari, K., Schleicher, R, Arndt, S., Falk, T. & Möller, S.
items.v: Poster presented at the 39th annual congress of the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Akustik (DAGA 2013), Merano, Italy
items.ab: We explore EEG and affective self-reports while listeners perceive speech under varying reverberation. Links between acoustic degradation, perceived quality, and affective state are analyzed via spectral features and ERP components. The results motivate multimodal QoE measures that integrate perceptual and emotional responses for reverberant speech scenarios.

items.ti: Single-trial analysis of the neural correlates of speech quality perception
items.a: Porbadnigk, A. K., Treder, M., Blankertz, B., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S., Curio, G. & Müller, K.-R.
items.v: J. Neural Eng., 10, 1–20
items.ab: This paper presents a single-trial EEG analysis approach to investigate neural correlates of speech quality perception. The results show that quality-related brain responses can be detected at the individual trial level, providing a more fine-grained method for studying auditory perception.

items.ti: NeuroPad: Use Cases For A Mobile Physiological Interface
items.a: Matthies, D. J.C., Antons, J.-N., Heidmann, F., Wettach, R. & Schleicher, R.
items.v: Poster presented at the 7th Nordic Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (NordiCHI 2012), Copenhagen, Denmark
items.ab: We present NeuroPad, a mobile device prototype capable of acquiring physiological signals such as EEG, ECG, and EDA in everyday contexts. Several use cases are described, including emotion-aware interaction, stress monitoring, and adaptive feedback systems. Results from early trials demonstrate feasibility and highlight opportunities for integrating physiological sensing into mobile HCI applications.

items.ti: Zum Einsatz von Elektroenzephalographie bei der Messung der Wahrnehmug gestörter Sprache
items.a: Möller, S., Antons, J.-N., Arndt, S., Porbadnigk, A. K. & Schleicher, R.
items.v: Paper presented at the 23rd Konferenz Elektronische Sprachsignalverarbeitung (ESSV 2012), Cottbus, Germany
items.ab: Der Beitrag beschreibt den Einsatz von Elektroenzephalographie (EEG) zur Untersuchung der Wahrnehmung gestörter Sprache. Es wird aufgezeigt, wie ereigniskorrelierte Potentiale Unterschiede in der Verarbeitung von Sprachsignalen mit variierender Qualität widerspiegeln. Erste Ergebnisse bestätigen, dass EEG-basierte Maße wertvolle Ergänzungen zu subjektiven Bewertungen liefern können.

items.ti: Too Tired for Calling? A Physiological Measure of Fatigue Caused by Bandwidth Limitations
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Arndt, S., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Poster presented at the 4th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2012), Yarra Valley, Australia
items.ab: We evaluate how bandwidth-induced quality reductions in speech communication affect user fatigue. Physiological measures including heart rate variability and blink activity are collected alongside subjective reports. Findings indicate that constrained bandwidth conditions lead to higher fatigue compared to full-bandwidth communication, emphasizing the importance of considering long-term effects of quality impairments.

items.ti: Perception of Low-Quality Videos Analyzed by Means of Electroencephalography
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Poster presented at the 4th Int. Workshop on Quality of Multimedia Experience (QoMEX 2012), Yarra Valley, Australia
items.ab: This study examines how low-quality video content is processed by the brain using EEG measures. Participants viewed videos of varying quality levels while their neural activity was recorded. Analysis reveals specific EEG patterns associated with perceptual strain and reduced engagement under degraded conditions, suggesting EEG as a valuable tool for objective QoE assessment.

items.ti: Correlating Physiological with Behavioural Data in Quality Research
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S., Scholler, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Paper presented at the Tagung experimentell arbeitender Psychologen (TEAP 2012), Mannheim, Germany
items.ab: This contribution explores the integration of physiological and behavioral data in multimedia quality research. By combining EEG, cardiovascular measures, and user task performance, the study demonstrates converging evidence of how quality degradations impact both perception and behavior. The approach underlines the benefits of multimodal assessment in QoE studies.

items.ti: Analyzing Speech Quality Perception using Electro-Encephalography
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Arndt, S., Möller, S., Porbadnigk, A. K. & Curio, G.
items.v: Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 6, 721–731
items.ab: This article investigates how EEG can be applied to analyze speech quality perception. The findings demonstrate that neural measures provide valuable insights into the perceptual processes underlying subjective quality assessments, establishing EEG as a complementary tool to traditional QoE methods.

items.ti: A Physiological Approach to Determine Video Quality
items.a: Arndt, S., Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Möller, S., Scholler, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Paper presented at the IEEE International Symposium on Multimedia (ISM 2011), Dana Point, CA, USA
items.ab: We propose a physiological methodology to assess perceived video quality by combining subjective ratings with EEG and autonomic measures. Results indicate that physiological responses correlate significantly with user judgments of quality, enabling objective prediction of Quality of Experience. The study highlights the potential of physiology-driven QoE assessment frameworks.

items.ti: Using ERPs to Assess the Processing of Words Under Broadcast Bit Rate Limitations
items.a: Porbadnigk, A. K., Antons, J.-N., Treder, M. S., Blankertz, B., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Poster presented at the Meeting of the Society of Applied Neurosciences (SAN 2011), Thessaloniki, Greece
items.ab: This poster presents an ERP study on how broadcast bit rate limitations influence word processing. Participants listened to spoken words transmitted under varying bit rate conditions while EEG responses were recorded. Distinct ERP components reflected differences in perceptual processing, indicating that neural measures can sensitively capture quality-related speech perception effects.

items.ti: Subjective Listening Tests and Neural Correlates of Speech Degradation in Case of Signal-correlated Noise
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Porbadnigk, A. K., Schleicher, R., Blankertz, B., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Paper presented at the 129th Audio Engineering Society Convention (129th AES Convention), San Francisco, CA, USA
items.ab: In this paper, we examine whether particularly sensitivity of the human cortex to reduction in speech quality is visible in the electroencephalogram (EEG) and whether these measures can be used to improve the behavioral assessment of speech quality. We degraded a speech stimulus (vowel/a/) in a scalable way and asked for a behavioural rating. In addition, the brain activity was measured with EEG. We trained classifiers, which were found capable of distinguishing between events which are seemingly similar at the behavioral level (ie, no button press), neurally, however, noise contamination is detected, possibly affecting the long-term contentment with the transmission quality.

items.ti: You think it's hi-fi – yet your brain might spot the difference: An EEG study on subconscious processing of noisy audio signals
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Porbadnigk, A. K., Schleicher, R., Blankertz, B., Möller, S. & Curio, Gabriel
items.v: Paper presented at the 10th Biannual Meeting of the German Society for Cognitive Science (KogWis 2010), Potsdam, Germany
items.ab: We investigate whether the brain discriminates between clean and mildly degraded audio even when listeners report no noticeable difference. EEG evidence reveals pre-attentive and decision-related ERP modulations for noisy signals, suggesting subconscious processing of subtle quality impairments and implications for objective audio quality assessment.

items.ti: Assessing the (Sub-)Conscious Processing of Noise based on ERPs
items.a: Porbadnigk, A. K., Antons, J.-N., Blankertz, B., Treder, M. S., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Poster presented at the Bernstein Conference on Computational Neuroscience (BCCN 2010), Berlin, Germany
items.ab: This poster presents an ERP paradigm to quantify conscious and pre-conscious processing of noise in speech. Differences in early sensory and later cognitive components across masking conditions reveal that noise alters auditory processing even without explicit awareness, offering sensitive biomarkers for perceived quality.

items.ti: Neural correlates of speech degradation – Subjective ratings and brain activation in case of signal-correlated noise
items.a: Antons, J.-N., Schleicher, R., Wolf, I., Porbadnigk, A. K., Blankertz, B., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Paper presented at the 3rd International Workshop on Perceptual Quality of Systems (PQS 2010), Bautzen, Germany
items.ab: We relate subjective judgments of speech quality under signal-correlated noise to neural activity measured with EEG. Degradation strength predicts both lower quality ratings and systematic changes in ERP morphology, establishing a link between perceived impairment and objective neurophysiological markers of auditory processing.

items.ti: Using ERPs for Assessing the (Sub)Conscious Perception of Noise
items.a: Porbadnigk, A. K., Antons, J.-N., Blankertz, B., Treder, M. S., Schleicher, R., Möller, S. & Curio, G.
items.v: Paper presented at the 32nd Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC 2010), Buenos Aires, Argentina
items.ab: We propose event-related potentials as objective indicators for (sub)conscious perception of noise in speech signals. The study demonstrates reliable ERP differences between clean and degraded conditions, supporting ERPs as complementary measures to subjective ratings for evaluating perceptual impact of noise.
